results.need: Feasibility summary: what trading Hyperliquid perps needs from a browser wallet (EVM signing)
results.endpoint: Signing flow: wallet eth_signTypedData_v4 for user-signed actions, plus a local agent key for L1 actions, both POSTed to /exchange
results.sample_fields: approveAgent action: {type:"approveAgent", hyperliquidChain:"Mainnet", signatureChainId:"0xa4b1", agentAddress, agentName, nonce}. Order action: {type:"order", orders:[{a:assetIndex, b:isBuy, p:"px", s:"sz", r:reduceOnly, t:{limit:{tif:"Gtc"|"Ioc"|"Alo"}}}], grouping:"na", builder?:{b:addr, f:tenthsOfBp}}
results.notes: FEASIBLE from a static site with no backend, but it needs an EVM wallet. Not done here: no signing or trading was tested; the steps below come from Hyperliquid's documented protocol. (1) Wallet: the user needs an EVM wallet (MetaMask, Rabby, or Phantom's EVM account) and EVM-only libraries (viem/ethers). A Solana-only wallet cannot trade or even be looked up. (2) Funding: USDC on Arbitrum is sent to the Hyperliquid bridge (0x2Df1c51E09aECF9cacB7bc98cB1742757f163dF7, 5 USDC minimum, about 1 min to credit). That is a wallet transaction the site can prompt for. Withdrawals use the user-signed withdraw3 action with a ~$1 fee. SOL can also come in through the Hyperunit bridge, but it lands as a spot asset, not perp USDC margin. (3) Signing: user actions (approveAgent, approveBuilderFee, usdSend, withdraw3, usdClassTransfer) are EIP-712 typed data with domain 'HyperliquidSignTransaction' and chainId 42161, so normal wallet popups work. Trading actions (order, cancel, modify, updateLeverage) use a 'phantom agent' signature: the action is msgpack-encoded with nonce and vault, keccak-hashed, then signed under domain 'Exchange' with chainId 1337. Wallets like MetaMask refuse that chainId mismatch. The standard pattern, which Hyperliquid's own UI and Axiom-style terminals use, is: the user signs approveAgent ONCE with their wallet, the site generates an agent private key in the browser (kept in localStorage or IndexedDB), and that key signs every order with no popups. That gives one-click trading. Agent keys can trade but cannot withdraw. (4) Revenue: builder codes let the site add a fee (field f, in tenths of a basis point, max 0.1% on perps) after the user signs approveBuilderFee once. (5) Libraries: @nktkas/hyperliquid (TypeScript, runs in the browser, includes signing helpers) or a hand-rolled version with @msgpack/msgpack plus viem, loadable from cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm. Order details: prices must respect 5 significant figures and the asset's szDecimals; asset index = position in the meta.universe array; market orders are IOC limit orders at a slippage-adjusted price. (6) Risks: storing agent keys in the browser has security implications, and Hyperliquid's terms restrict US and some other jurisdictions (the API does not block by IP, but the operator carries the compliance risk). Overall: read-only perps data (screener, charts, book, positions by address) is fully usable today with no keys. Trading is technically possible client-side but adds an EVM wallet requirement alongside the Solana pump.fun flow.

results.need: Top holders list (largest token accounts) for a mint
results.rate_limit: Method is disabled: always HTTP 429 'Too many requests for a specific RPC call' with x-ratelimit-method-limit: 0, from any Origin (or none). Also fails for the SOL mint.
results.notes: Do not use it. The public RPC (operated by Triton One) also allowlists Origins. Only https://solana.com, https://www.solana.com, https://explorer.solana.com and https://faucet.solana.com get a matching ACAO. Every other Origin tested (example.com, *.netlify.app, localhost, 127.0.0.1, claude.ai, *.claudeusercontent.com, github.io, pump.fun, jup.ag, solscan.io, file://) gets HTTP 403 'Access forbidden' on every method, even getSlot. That 403 carries ACAO '*', so a browser can read the error. The OPTIONS preflight from example.com passes, but the POST itself is 403. With Origin 'null' or no Origin the call gets through, but ACAO comes back as the literal 'backend_traffic', which a browser rejects.

results.need: Candles (OHLCV) by pool, GeckoTerminal: limits, timeframes, paging
results.rate_limit: Public, no key, but frequently returned HTTP 429 at about one request every 2-10s from this IP (parallel agents may share it; the documented limit is about 30/min). The 429 body is from CoinGecko, carries NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (a browser sees an opaque CORS error) and has retry-after: 0. 200 responses are cache-control max-age=30, s-maxage=60. No x-ratelimit headers.
results.sample_fields: data.attributes.ohlcv_list = [[ts_sec, open, high, low, close, volume_usd], ...] newest-first; meta.base{name,symbol,address}, meta.quote{symbol,address}
results.notes: limit max 1000 (1001 returns 400 'must be ... <= 1000'). Allowed aggregates: minute 1/5/15, hour 1/4/12, day 1 (other values return 400, e.g. 'Allowed values: 1, 5, 15'). The timeframe=second endpoint returns 401 'exclusive to Paid plan'. before_timestamp (unix seconds) is EXCLUSIVE: before_timestamp=1790375820 returned newest 1790375760, so page backwards with before_timestamp=oldest_ts and no dedupe is needed. The public API only serves the past 180 days (older before_timestamp returns 401 'only access data from the past 180 days'); day returned 183 candles and hour limit=1000 went back about 41 days; minute data with before_timestamp 7 days back worked (1000 candles). By default only intervals with trades are returned (the HATCH pumpswap pool gave 48 candles); include_empty_intervals=true fills gaps with flat candles at the previous close with volume 0 (81 candles). currency=token returns SOL-denominated prices; token=quote returns the SOL/USD candles. Verified on the pumpswap pool GuwoKCn33WVKy2ptj92frc4wjQDDQzUCGJrLRnv8NDRT (HATCH/SOL, created 2026-10-03T13:56Z) and the Orca SOL/USDC pool Czfq3xZZDmsdGdUyrNLtRhGc47cXcZtLG4crryfu44zE.

results.need: Candles by token mint, Jupiter (keyless, covers bonding curve plus migrated pool in one series)
results.rate_limit: No 429 in a 40-request rapid burst and no rate-limit headers. cache-control public, max-age=5. ACAO reflects the request Origin (https://example.com) with access-control-allow-credentials: true.
results.sample_fields: candles[] = {time (unix sec), open, high, low, close, volume (USD for quote=usd)}, ascending oldest-first; the response has no other top-level keys
results.notes: BEST keyless option. The series is keyed by mint, so for 8oEz...pump it spans 13:16 (bonding curve) to now (pumpswap) in one stream, with no stitching. Its volume matched GT's bonding-curve candle (~1762 vs 1760 USD). The 'to' param is REQUIRED and in milliseconds (omitting it returns 400; passing seconds returns an empty candles array). 'to' is exclusive (candles with time < to), so page backwards with to=oldest.time*1000. candles cap = 7000 (asking for 8000 or 10000 returned 7000). Intervals 1_SECOND, 15_SECOND, 30_SECOND, 1_MINUTE, 3_MINUTE, 5_MINUTE, 15_MINUTE, 30_MINUTE, 1_HOUR, 2_HOUR, 4_HOUR, 8_HOUR, 12_HOUR, 1_DAY, 1_WEEK and 1_MONTH all work; 3_DAY returns 400. type=mcap returns market-cap OHLC (2883 USD for HATCH); type=foo returns 400. quote=native returns SOL-denominated prices and volume; quote=sol returns 400 'Invalid quote.'. Deep history: SOL 1_MINUTE with to=200 days ago returned data, and 1_SECOND with to=30 days ago returned data. Gaps where there were no trades are skipped (not filled). This is an undocumented frontend data API, so it could change. The old routes fe-api.jup.ag/api/v1/charts/{mint} and datapi.jup.ag/v1/charts/{mint} return 404.
